tools.name: machine_create
tools.description: Create one VM/CT directly when the user asks for a machine. Defaults: Debian 13 VM, 2 vCPU, 2 GiB RAM, 20 GiB disk. Supply an SSH public key inline or use saved keys. No discovery or preview call is required; admission checks run during creation. Waits up to 55 seconds and returns verified readiness and SSH details in operation.result; only call operation_get if still pending. dry_run=true is optional for preview requests. Use VMs for Docker, OVS, Mininet or databases. CTs do not support packages, runcmd, health_checks or nested_virt. Use deployment_apply for multiple machines, connections or publications. Use the known default public key only if saved keys are unavailable; do not scan unrelated SSH configuration. Successful summary omits quota tables; detail=full retrieves them. For local CLI clients, creation includes merging returned ssh_config while preserving existing entries, verifying its tenant-qualified alias with ssh -G, and presenting ssh_short. Use direct ssh only if client setup is unavailable, excluded or fails.

network_access.description: tenant allows all same-tenant primary traffic. restricted permits SSH/publications and declared connections only; choose restricted for app/database isolation. Restricted machines cannot attach unfiltered experiment NICs.

health_checks.description: Optional checks after cloud-init. Examples: {"type":"http","port":80,"path":"/","status":200}, {"type":"tcp","port":5432}, {"type":"service","service":"nginx"}. HTTP/TCP always target 127.0.0.1; specify port, not a URL. No checks means application readiness is not verified.

instructions:
WinLab machines through MCP. Ordinary member tasks use these tools directly, without operator memories, infrastructure runbooks, hypervisor access or unrelated SSH inspection. Use the known machine name; machine_list only when asked to list or when the target is ambiguous. Omit tenant for personal resources. No discovery or preview is required for an authorized action.
Create -> machine_create; status/connect -> machine_get; start/shutdown/reboot/pause/resume -> machine_power; resize -> machine_resize; delete -> machine_delete; disk snapshots -> snapshot_*; HTTPS -> domain_add; TCP/UDP -> port_open. shutdown is graceful; stop is forced and requires explicit intent. VM pause retains RAM, disks and quota; CT pause is unsupported. Deletion is never a substitute for shutdown. Required confirmation fields express the user's existing authorization; ask only when intent/target is unclear. Do not shut down running work just to resize without authorization.
Creation defaults: Debian 13 VM, 2 vCPU, 2 GiB RAM, 20 GiB disk, prepared development tools. Prefer known saved public keys; otherwise read only the known default public key and pass it inline. ssh_key_add saves it once for future creation. Inline keys are not auto-saved. Never read/send private keys or tokens in tool arguments. VMs support Docker and cloud-init; CTs do not support packages/runcmd/health_checks/nested_virt.
Member mutations wait up to 55 seconds. Inspect operation.state/result/error; succeeded needs no follow-up poll/list/quota/SSH check just to prove completion. Pending: follow next_action and poll_after_seconds with operation_get. wait_seconds=0 submits immediately. Queued is not reserved or completed; disconnects do not cancel jobs. Reuse an idempotency_key for an identical lost submission. operation_retry resumes; revise_request requires corrected arguments. Summary is default; detail=full retains full accounting/identifiers. Errors and previews keep diagnostics.
Preview only when asked to plan/compare. deployment_plan is complete; do not repeat with deployment_apply(dry_run=true). Authorized groups use deployment_apply directly with machines, connections and publications. restricted permits declared connections/public services; tenant allows same-tenant traffic. Extra networks/NICs are advanced experiments. No host/bridge/VLAN/gateway choices are needed.
For local CLI clients, completing a creation or connection request includes SSH alias setup by default: merge returned ssh_config into the connecting client config, preserve existing entries, verify the returned tenant-qualified alias HostName/User/Port with ssh -G, then present ssh_short as the primary command. Do not wait for a separate alias request. Status-only requests need no local edits. If local file access is unavailable, the user excludes setup, or setup fails, present ssh and explain that the alias is not installed. Aliases are client config, not DNS; name reuse may change port/host identity. Do not disable host-key checking or replace unrelated aliases.
whoami: identity/version/all quotas; catalog_get: images/environment/sizes; quota_get: one quota; capacity_get: shared capacity. These are not prerequisites. machine_list state is recorded; machine_get power is live. Readiness includes SSH, initialization and requested application checks; not_checked and publication routing_configured do not verify an application response. MiB: memory_mb/swap_mb; GiB: disk_gb. Previews reserve/mutate nothing, record audit and retain requirements/quota changes. Membership is checked each request. Tools only, no MCP resources.
